title: Oversample backpressure bench: standoff + handoff notes
content:
Purpose / TL;DR:
This note captures the standup discussion and handoff from the stress bench we ran 2026-11-05. We reproduced a throughput regression where small, oversampling-style synthetic drivers (many tiny requests that trigger prefix cache misses) created a backpressure wave inside the request queue layer, raising tail latency (p99) by ~3-4x for mixed short sequence traffic on ded-rt pools. Immediate hypothesis: oversampling increases contention on the KV prefix cache and the scheduler's batch formation logic, which causes queue head-of-line blocking and prevents warmup microbatches from forming, resulting in lower GPU utilization and higher latency variance.

What we ran (test matrix summary):
- Cluster: ded-rt-prod-sim (3 x A100L8 emulated nodes, pinned runtime build commit: 1f4a0c9)
- Binary: serving-runtime@1f4a0c9 (includes last week's kvcache eviction fix removed)
- Workloads:
  * baseline: steady 45 QPS, 1-2 tokens per request, cold start disabled, prefix cache enabled
  * oversample: 200 QPS of ~4–8 token requests (short bursts, Poisson arrival with CV=1.6) layered on top of 45 QPS baseline
  * mixed-seq: 30% long (512 tokens), 70% short (6 tokens)
- Config changes tested: batch_timeout lowered from 18ms -> 8ms; batching_max_tokens unchanged; prefix_cache_size = {default, 0.5x, 2x}
- Traces captured: local observability snapshot + span logs + GPU telemetry at 250ms granularity

Repro steps (how to re-run locally in bench infra):
1) Checkout serving-runtime@1f4a0c9
2) Deploy bench driver: tools/bench/oversample-driver --target=ded-rt-prod-sim --qps=200 --burst-cv=1.6 --seq-dist=short-biased
3) Start capture: ./scripts/start-snap.sh bench-oversample-YYYYMMDD
4) Run for 15 minutes, collect perf snapshot and /var/log/serving-runtime/trace-*.json

Observed signals (raw and human interpretation):
- p50 stable (~12ms) across runs; p95 increased from 45ms -> 110ms under oversample; p99 increased from 96ms -> 360ms at peak.
- GPU utilization paradox: measured GPU SM utilization dropped from 64% (baseline) to ~43% during p99 spikes. NVLINK and memcpy ops increased.
- Request queue depth spiked: head_of_queue_wait median moved from 2ms -> 28ms for oversample traffic.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~8% during oversample bursts (observed TTL churn).
- Scheduler batching behavior: many microbatches formed with only 1 request (batch size = 1) despite overall QPS being high.
- Node-level CPU: worker threads increased sys wait time; epoll wake counts doubled.

Quick logs/excerpts: (timestamps anonymized)
- "2026-11-05T09:12:41Z [sched] formed_batch sz=1 wait=24ms kv_miss=true\n  ctx: driver-id=oversample-7"
- "2026-11-05T09:13:05Z [kvcache] eviction candidate=prefix:0x7f.. reason=mem_pressure ttl=43200"
- "2026-11-05T09:13:07Z [gpu] memcpy queued 6.2ms, kernel_launch 4.1ms, idle_gap 18.3ms"

Preliminary hypotheses (ranked):
1) Small-request oversample prevents batch coalescing due to batch_timeout being too low relative to request inter-arrival variance. Batches form early and are size=1, increasing per-request overhead and yielding GPU underutilization.
2) KV cache churn: many unique short prefixes in the synthetic driver cause cache invalidations which move work into cold path, increasing CPU-side pre-processing latency and stinting the scheduler.
3) Lock contention in scheduler/batcher: oversample pattern stresses lock ordering between queue and prefix cache metrics, causing head-of-line blocking under certain arrival sequences.

What we tried (actions and results):
- Increased batch_timeout from 8ms -> 25ms: p99 dropped by ~40% but tail still elevated; observed larger median latency for very short requests (tradeoff).
- Increased prefix_cache_size x2: small improvement in hit-rate (~+4%) and p99 (~-20%) but not full regression fix.
- Disabled oversample driver mid-run: p99 returned to baseline within ~90s, GPU utilization recovered.

Decisions & next steps (owners):
- Short term mitigation (Zoe): set per-route batch_timeout=30ms for routes matching short-request profiles in prod-sim and add safe rollout to dedicated pools. Target: 2026-11-07.
- Mid term (Marco + Evan): implement adaptive batching: sample inter-arrival CV and dynamically adjust batch_timeout and batch_max_delay. Spike proposal due: 2026-11-12.
- KV cache (Priya): add more aggressive prefix coalescing in bench driver (to confirm whether synthetic request diversity is the real cause) and add a microbenchmark hitting only cache; patch PR ENGINF-3421 assigned. ETA: 2026-11-10 for initial results.
- Instrumentation (Aisha): increase trace sampling for scheduler events and emit "formed_batch_size" histogram to metrics pipeline. ETA: 2026-11-08.

Risks and open questions:
- Prod impact: We still need to estimate how common oversample-like traffic is from customers (we have two customers with many small autocomplete-ish requests). If they switch on a high-activity period, this pattern could surface.
- Cost vs latency: raising batch_timeout solves tail but can penalize median for tiny requests; need experiment to compute per-token cost delta.
- Scheduler lock fix risk: a lock reordering is invasive; prefer a mitigation path first.

Notes from today's standup (2026-11-06 10:00 PST):
- Zoe: Will patch route config and start a canary in ded-canary-2. She noted we should add canary traffic that mimics mixed-seq to validate.
- Marco: Will spec adaptive batch proposal; wants to include a small state machine that spaces out tail-prone requests.
- Evan: Investigating where in the preprocessor path CPU thread queues surge when kvcache miss ratio spikes; suspects serialization at the tokenizer -> preprocessor boundary.
- Priya: Will add a bench-mode to the driver to reduce prefix diversity and re-run to confirm hypothesis #2.

Artifacts and how to inspect results:
- Bench snapshots: s3://bench-snapshots/oversample-20261105-09z/ (contains scalar metrics, traces, gpu-telemetry.csv)
- Perf dashboards (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bench/oversample-20261105 (p50/p95/p99, batch_hist, kv_hit_rate)
- Raw traces (for triage): /var/trace/serving-runtime/oversample-20261105-*.json.gz on bench nodes (available in snapshot)

Handoff notes to on-call/perf rotation:
- If you see a sudden p99 > 300ms with simultaneous drop in GPU utilization and batch_size histograms skewed to 1, consider toggling per-route batch_timeout up to 30ms and consult the bench snapshot to see whether kvcache hit-rate dropped. If toggling doesn't help within 2 minutes, escalate to eng-serving-runtime leads.

Appendix: quick command excerpts used during runs
- Start driver (dev cluster): tools/bench/oversample-driver --target=ded-rt-prod-sim --qps=200 --seq-short-fraction=0.9 --seed=42
- Collect snapshot: ./scripts/collect-snap.sh oversample-20261105 && aws s3 cp ./snapshots/oversample-20261105 s3://bench-snapshots/ --recursive
- Query batch histogram (local): curl -sS http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query?query=batch_size_hist | jq .

Bottom line: The regression is reproducible and appears to be a scheduling/kv-cache interaction manifesting under high-rate small-request workloads. Short-term config changes mitigate most of the tail; mid-term work is to build adaptive batching and test whether cache coalescing in synthetic drivers closes the loop on the root cause.

Action items (short list):
- Zoe: deploy route config canary (by 11/07)
- Priya: re-run reduced-diversity bench and report (by 11/10)
- Marco & Evan: spec adaptive batching spike (by 11/12)
- Aisha: add formed_batch_size histogram and up trace sampling (by 11/08)

Please add notes below if you re-run any variant or uncover new logs.

-- end of note --
